children: India's three state-run fuel retailers earned a combined standalone net profit of  ₹30,106 crore in the July-September quarter, nearly 39 per cent of their annual earnings, after a refining margin boost and inventory gains helped more than offset losses on fuel sales and a mounting unpaid LPG subsidy bill.

The combined profit of Indian Oil Corporation (IOC), Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd (HPCL) is 68.3 per cent more than their earnings in the same period last year and a swing from a combined loss of about Rs 18,150 crore in the previous April-June quarter, according to company filings.
The July-September quarter alone equals about 39 per cent of the three companies' combined FY26 (April 2025 to March 2026 financial year) profit of  ₹77,281 crore.
The boost in earnings came despite petrol and diesel prices remaining on freeze since May and unchanged domestic LPG rates since March, despite a surge in benchmark prices and input crude oil rates.
The three companies were till last month losing  ₹4-5 a litre on petrol and  ₹18-20 on diesel, industry sources said.

IOC Director (Finance) Anuj Jain at an investor call on Saturday said under-recoveries or losses on LPG were  ₹184 per cylinder in September, which rose to  ₹229 in October and are expected to further go up to  ₹309 in November and  ₹370 per cylinder in December.

While petrol and diesel prices are deregulated and any loss has to be borne by the companies, LPG continues to be a regulated commodity with the government expected to make good on the difference between retail price and actual cost.
With government subsidies not coming in time, the three companies accumulated under-recoveries on fuel totalling  ₹67,900 crore at the end of September, according to the filings.
IOC reported  ₹32,505.69 crore of under-recovery, BPCL  ₹17,334.40 crore and HPCL  ₹18,048.82 crore.
The earnings boost was primarily because of high refining margins and inventory gains.

IOC accounted for the bulk of the September-quarter earnings, reporting its highest-ever standalone quarterly net profit of  ₹ 21,630 crore, almost three times the  ₹7,610 crore recorded a year earlier. The figure alone represented nearly 59 pr cent of the company's full-year FY26 profit of  ₹36,802 crore.

title: Oil PSUs clock ₹30,106 cr Q2 profit, near 39% of last year’s earnings
